title: 2005 AMC 12B 12
statement: The quadratic equation \(x^2 + mx + n = 0\) has roots that are twice those of \(x^2 + px + m = 0,\) and none of \(m,\) \(n,\) and \(p\) is zero. What is the value of \(\dfrac{n}{p}?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) be the roots of \(x^2 + px + m = 0,\) so \(m = r_1 r_2\) and \(p = -(r_1 + r_2).\)

The roots of \(x^2 + mx + n = 0\) are \(2r_1\) and \(2r_2,\) so \(n = 4r_1 r_2\) and \(m = -2(r_1 + r_2).\)

Then \(n = 4m\) and \(m = 2p,\) which gives \(p = \dfrac{m}{2},\) so \[ \dfrac{n}{p} = \dfrac{4m}{\tfrac{m}{2}} = 8. \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let \(r_1, r_2\) be the roots of \(x^2 + px + m = 0\); the other equation has roots \(2r_1, 2r_2\)
Write \(m, n, p\) in terms of \(r_1 r_2\) and \(r_1 + r_2\) using Vieta’s formulas
